column2:
[Root.GetTitledFirstName],

The people of [target_province.GetName] have dragged their midwife before me. They say her herbs are poison, that she speaks to crows, and that three babes she delivered this spring were born with the mark of the Changer. She weeps and calls on Shallya.

The crowd wants fire. I await your judgement.

[witch_hunter.GetTitledFirstName]
Burn her. Better one innocent than a village lost.
Spare her. The Order judges, not the mob.
Have her examined by learned men.
The examiners find a hedge witch after all.
She is only a midwife, and the province remembers your fairness.

[Root.GetTitledFirstName],

Beneath a mill in [target_province.GetName] we found a shrine to the Ruinous Powers: a silver altar, bones, and walls covered in markings that hurt the eye. The worshippers fled before we came.

What shall be done with it?

[witch_hunter.GetTitledFirstName]
Burn it, salt the ground, and pray.
The silver at least can serve Sigmar. Melt it down.
Copy the markings. To know the enemy is to defeat him.
Someone saw you poring over heretical symbols.

[Root.GetTitledFirstName],

The purge of [target_province.GetName] has gone on too long for its people. Last night a mob gathered outside our lodgings with torches, crying that we burn their neighbours to fill the Order's coffers. Stones were thrown. One of my men was hurt.

[witch_hunter.GetTitledFirstName]
Hang the ringleaders. Defiance of the Order is heresy.
Pay for the damage and calm them down.
The Order has learned of a mutant hiding among the faithful. Find it and deal with it.
Informants name a member of a cult of the Ruinous Powers. Expose the cell.
Something dead walks near the realm. Find its master and destroy it.

Word comes from the Order: a mutant hides among the people near [Root.GetLiege.GetTitledFirstName]'s lands. It goes by the name [whunter_quarry.GetFirstName], and those who have seen beneath its hood speak of scales and too many teeth.\n\nYou are to hunt it down. How you do so is your own affair.
You have tracked [whunter_quarry.GetFirstName] to a cellar where it thought itself safe. By lantern light the thing is plainly mutated, and plainly afraid.\n\nIt begs for its life.
Drag it before its liege for judgement.
Let the wretch go. It has harmed no one.

The Order's informants name [whunter_quarry.GetTitledFirstName] as a member of a cult of the Ruinous Powers. Where there is one cultist there are more, and they meet in secret.\n\nYou are to find the cell and expose it.
You have learned where the cell meets: tonight, in a crypt beneath a shuttered chapel. [whunter_quarry.GetTitledFirstName] will be there.\n\nThe question is how you go in.
Storm the gathering with steel and fire.
Slip in among them in a borrowed robe.
Report [whunter_quarry.GetFirstName] to [whunter_quarry.GetHerHis] liege and let the law handle it.
The cultists see through you and spread rumours that you are one of them.

Graves lie open near [Root.GetLiege.GetTitledFirstName]'s lands, and the dead have been seen walking. The Order believes [whunter_quarry.GetFirstName] is behind it: a necromancer, or worse.\n\nOnly a seasoned hunter is sent after such prey.
The trail ends at an old crypt. The air is cold and smells of grave dirt, and something moves in the dark below. [whunter_quarry.GetFirstName] is down there.
Stake and fire. Go in now.
Seal the crypt with Sigmar's rites first.

The Council has spoken: [From.GetTitledFirstName] can no longer give orders nor carry out [From.GetHerHis] duties. The Order needs a master who can stand.\n\nShall [From.GetSheHe] be relieved of command?
Relieve [From.GetHerHim]. A new master will be found.
[From.GetSheHe] has earned the right to keep [From.GetHerHis] seat.
The Order wants its blades sharp and its faith sharper. Test yourself against a fellow member.
Go among the people and remind them what waits for those who stray.

A senior brother of the Order has noticed that you grow slack. Steel rusts and so does faith, he says, and he has paired you with [whunter_sparring_partner.GetTitledFirstName] to put both to the test.

[whunter_sparring_partner.GetTitledFirstName] waits for you in the yard of the chapter house, two blunted swords and a well-thumbed copy of the Deus Sigmar on the bench beside [whunter_sparring_partner.GetHerHim].\n\n'Steel or scripture, brother?'
Scripture. Test me on the catechism.

The Order sends word: the people of [whunter_sermon_province.GetName] grow lax in their faith, and where faith weakens the Ruinous Powers creep in. You are to preach to them and remind them what they face.

The square of [whunter_sermon_province.GetName] is full. Merchants, farmers, beggars and a few nobles in fine cloaks have come to hear the witch hunter speak. They are waiting.\n\nWhat will you tell them?
Thunder against the Ruinous Powers and those who serve them!
Point out [whunter_named_suspect.GetTitledFirstName] in the crowd. Let all see the suspect.
Preach mercy, and vigilance. Watch your neighbours, but do not hate them.
The crowd turns into a mob and the sermon ends in a riot.
The accused was a true servant of the Ruinous Powers. The Order is pleased.

Solkan is the Lord of Vengeance, a cold god of Law who does not forgive. His cult is small and feared even by those it protects: its priests preach that Chaos must be answered with fire, and that mercy is only another door left open. Most of his faithful are witch hunters, and the Templars of Solkan carry his creed from court to court.

The Holy Inquisition answers to the Great Temple of Myrmidia in Magritta. It hunts heretics, witches and Chaos worshippers across Estalia and Tilea with the patience of a siege: it gathers testimony, holds tribunals, and burns only when the verdict is certain. Its Grand Inquisitor sits in Magritta, and the Knights of the Blazing Sun ride when he calls.

The Grand Inquisitor leads the Holy Inquisition from Magritta. When he dies, the Inquisitor-General with the strongest claim takes his seat, and those who serve in Magritta itself stand closest to it.

The Templars of Solkan are few, and they like it that way. They keep no great temple and answer to no prince. They go where heresy is rumoured, and they leave ash behind them. The Border Princes, who have no order of their own, often send for them, and most Templars come to worship the Lord of Vengeance himself.
The Master of Vengeance leads the Templars of Solkan. He is chosen for his zeal, not his birth.
The Court Inquisitor speaks for the Holy Inquisition of Myrmidia at court. He watches the household, gathers testimony, and goes out to purge any province touched by Chaos.
The Court Templar is a Templar of Solkan sworn to this court. He hunts witches, heretics and the servants of Chaos, and he does not ask permission twice.

Send this courtier to a witch hunter chapterhouse. Four years of fasting, scripture, interrogation and the pyre will harden him. He comes home a witch hunter and takes your Court Witch Hunter seat, or Court Inquisitor or Court Templar where the Inquisition or the Templars of Solkan answer for your lands, if a seat is still free.
He leaves court for about four years and comes home a witch hunter.
This character is away at a witch hunter chapterhouse, learning the trade of fire and question.
Put this accused prisoner before a tribunal of the Holy Inquisition.
Inquisitors-General may put an accused prisoner before a tribunal and burn, convert or acquit them.
Is a cultist, a suspect, a mutant, a dark sorcerer, a condemned mage or a heretic
Call the Knights of the Blazing Sun
The Knights of the Blazing Sun, Myrmidia's own order, will ride as the Grand Inquisitor's escort for two years.
The Grand Inquisitor may call 300 Knights of the Blazing Sun and 500 men-at-arms as his escort for two years.
300 Knights of the Blazing Sun and 500 men-at-arms join you where you stand. They ride home after two years.
A Templar of Solkan swears before his god that the guilty will not escape him. For three years he thinks of nothing else.
Templars may swear an Oath of Vengeance: more martial skill and combat strength for three years, at the cost of diplomacy.
Burn the taint of Chaos out of the province you stand in. Its lord will not thank you.
Vindicators may purge the province they stand in by fire, clearing Chaos taints and exposing any cultist at its lord's court.

The Border Princes have no order of witch hunters of their own. Send for one. A Myrmidian, Estalian or Tilean lord gets the Holy Inquisition. A Sigmarite, Ulrican or Taalite lord usually gets the Order of Sigmar, sometimes a Templar or an Inquisitor. Anyone else gets the Templars of Solkan.
A witch hunter of the chapter that answers joins your court and takes the empty court seat.
If your lord sides with you, you gain §G100§! currency.
If your lord sides with the other hunter, you lose §R100§! currency and some prestige.
If the Seeker finds the prisoner innocent, they go free.
If the Seeker finds the prisoner guilty, all will know it.
A Vindicator of Solkan burned the taint of Chaos out of this province. The ash is still warm.
The Knights of the Blazing Sun rode at this Grand Inquisitor's call. They will not come again soon.
The Ordo Fidelis, who watch the watchers, know this lord shielded a witch hunter who went too far. Word gets around.
Shielded me from the Ordo Fidelis
Handed me to the Ordo Fidelis
A heavy signet of the Holy Inquisition, carved with Myrmidia's spear and eagle. Its seal on a verdict means fire.
A short iron rod worn black with use. The Templars of Solkan mark the condemned with it before the pyre, so that their god will know them.

The tribunal sits in a cold stone hall. [tribunal_accused.GetTitledFirstName] stands in chains before you, and the clerks have filled three ledgers with testimony: neighbours who saw lights at night, a servant who found the wrong book, a confession given on the second day of questioning. The court of the Holy Inquisition waits for your verdict.
Let them recant before Myrmidia and live.
The evidence does not hold. Release them.

Your Templars go through the province with torches and iron. Barns where cults met are burned, a shrine to nothing anyone will name is pulled down, and in the cellar of the lord's own house you find [purge_cultist.GetTitledFirstName] kneeling before a daubed altar. The servant of Chaos does not run. There is nowhere left to run to.
Your Templars go through the province with torches and iron. Barns where cults met are burned and the road shrines are cleansed with fire. Whatever hid here has fled or died. Only ash remains.
Let their lord judge them. He will know we know.

A rider in black arrives at your gate with a writ sealed in grey wax. The Templars of Solkan have heard your call. [chapter_envoy.GetTitledFirstName] does not kneel, does not smile, and asks only where the heretics are.

An Inquisitor of Myrmidia arrives with two clerks and a chest of ledgers. The Holy Inquisition has heard your call. [chapter_envoy.GetTitledFirstName] bows correctly and asks for a list of everyone at court, with their birthplaces.

A witch hunter of the Order of Sigmar arrives in a wide-brimmed hat, two pistols at his belt. The Order has heard your call. [chapter_envoy.GetTitledFirstName] takes one look at your court and asks for a room near the kitchens, where the gossip is best.

A sledge-rider in a grey fur coat arrives with a sealed letter from Kislev. The Chekist does not forget its own, however far south they settle. [chapter_envoy.GetTitledFirstName] opens a ledger already half full of names from your lands and asks which of them you would like explained.
Welcome. There is work for you here.

A rider in grey stops at your gate and will not get down. [wandering_hunter.GetTitledFirstName], Templar of Solkan, has followed a trail of heresy into your lands. Solkan's law needs no invitation, [wandering_hunter.GetSheHe] says, but it will need a roof, a table and your leave to burn whom it must.

An Inquisitor of Myrmidia has come a long way from Magritta. [wandering_hunter.GetTitledFirstName] presents letters from the Grand Inquisitor, asks for rooms, a clerk and a cellar that locks, and makes it plain that refusing the Holy Inquisition is itself a matter for inquiry.

A hunter in a wolf-pelt or a mantle of leaves walks out of the forest and asks to see you. [wandering_hunter.GetTitledFirstName] has hunted beast-witches and grove-poisoners for the old gods half a lifetime, and would serve a lord who lets [wandering_hunter.GetHerHim] keep doing it.

A witch hunter with a scarred face and a satchel of warrants rides into your court. [wandering_hunter.GetTitledFirstName] has burned witches from the Reik to the Black Mountains and offers to burn yours, for bed, board and a free hand.

A quiet Kislevite in a plain grey coat is waiting in your hall before anyone saw him arrive. [wandering_hunter.GetTitledFirstName] serves the Chekist, and the Chekist keeps watch over every son and daughter of the Motherland, at home or abroad. He asks for a room, a stove and the names of everyone who visits you.
My lands need no hunters. Ride on.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has come home from the chapterhouse. [From.GetSheHe] left court a courtier and returns thinner, quieter and with eyes that linger on everyone a moment too long. The chapter has made a witch hunter of [From.GetHerHim].
Welcome home. There is work to do.

[rival_hunter.GetTitledFirstName] of another chapter has claimed the case you were building: the miller's widow, the cellar, the black candles. They say your chapter has no authority here, and that you should hand over your notes and stand aside.
Take it. We serve the same cause.
This case is mine. Step aside.
Our lord will decide whose it is.

You have watched [lax_hunter.GetTitledFirstName] for months. A witch hunter who drinks at noon, sleeps late, and lets the accused go home for supper. Solkan does not forgive weakness in those who serve Law. Should anyone?
I will name them before the court.

A band of hunters in grey wolf-pelts rides into your court, the white wolf of Ulric on their shields. They track a beast-witch who has led a herd of Beastmen out of the deep forest, and the trail leads across your lands. Their captain asks for leave to hunt, and men to ride with him.
I will ride with you myself.
Hunt. And leave me one of your best.

Wardens of Taal, in green cloaks and antlered hoods, come to your hall. A witch has poisoned a sacred grove in your forests, and the trees bleed black sap and the deer lie dead in rings. They ask for leave to hunt her through your woods, and for a guide who knows them.
The forests are open to you.
Take my best huntsman as your guide.

A woman in grey with the scales of Verena at her throat asks for an audience. She is a Seeker of Truth and Justice, and she has heard of [seeker_accused.GetTitledFirstName], who waits in your dungeon on charges of witchcraft. She asks to examine the evidence before sentence is passed. "Justice that burns the innocent," she says, "feeds Chaos better than any cult."
My court, my justice. Good day.

A quiet man in a plain coat shows you a seal you have never seen and will not see again. He speaks for the Ordo Fidelis, who watch the witch hunters, and he has come for [cruel_hunter.GetTitledFirstName]. Twelve burned on rumour alone, he says. Children among them. The Ordo wants the hunter.
Take them. I want no part of it.
Perhaps the records could be... lost.

The Templars of Solkan do not ask their brothers to worship the Lord of Vengeance, but in the long nights on the road the old prayers sound different. [Root.GetFirstName] has hunted in Solkan's name for years. Perhaps it is time to kneel to him.
Solkan is the only god who does not forgive. I will serve him.
I hunt for my own god.
An Inquisitor of the Holy Inquisition of Myrmidia. Patient, learned and merciless, the Inquisition seeks out heresy in Estalia and Tilea with ledgers, questions and, in the end, fire.
A Templar of Solkan, the Lord of Vengeance. The Templars wander the Old World and answer heresy with the sword and the pyre. They do not forgive and they do not forget.

Strange lights are seen at night beneath the old wine cellars of [cabal_province.GetName]. Hooded figures come and go before dawn, the chanting can be heard through the floorboards, and a beggar who went to look was found with his eyes put out. Your people beg you to root out this cabal before something answers its call.
Hire a witch hunter, whatever it costs.
Witch hunters cause more trouble than any cabal.
